title: Pre-Analysis — Corrosion-Resistant Seat Track Splice Straps, Stations 41 to 48
abstract: Closed pre-analysis for the corrosion-resistant splice strap change at the cabin seat track joints, raised after galley and lavatory drainage findings on early aircraft in the forward cabin.

sections.objective: Work out what the change of splice strap material and fastener finish at the seat track joints costs in cabin downtime and what it collides with in the forward cabin floor. The strap change itself is small; the concern was the access it needs. Every cabin item bonded, clipped or routed across the floor panel joints between stations 41 and 48 had to be identified before the embodiment estimate could be trusted.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and none were blocking. The corrosion inspection task on the same joints is the one that mattered commercially: it already opens the floor at exactly the stations the strap change works on, and aligning the two turns a separate cabin-out visit into a task added to a scheduled inspection. The photoluminescent escape path marking is bonded across the floor panel joint line and cannot be lifted and refitted, so a strip length has to be replaced on every aircraft touched. The flight deck display work in the forward cabin zone shares the same floor access, and one operator had both scheduled in different visits. Nothing in the strap change affects the seat track load path, so no re-substantiation was required.
sections.next_steps: Write the embodiment instruction so it can be accomplished during the existing corrosion inspection rather than as a standalone visit. Add the escape path marking strip to the material list as a consumable rather than a reusable item. Flag the forward cabin floor access overlap to fleet planning so operators can group the work, and give them the panel list rather than a station range so the grouping can be checked against a layout. Record in the design justification that the strap change does not touch the seat track load path, so the question is not reopened at the next revision. Close the order without a second round.

similarity_seeds: corrosion at a fastened floor joint under a galley drain path
cabin work that requires the floor panels to be lifted between two stations

tasks.title: Identify every cabin item crossing the floor joints at stations 41 to 48
Align the strap change with the existing corrosion inspection
Assess cabin monument and marking reinstatement cost

expected_findings.rationale: The corrosion inspection opens the same floor panels at the same stations on a scheduled interval. Accomplishing the strap change during that inspection removes an entire cabin-out visit from the retrofit cost, and the inspection itself becomes redundant on post-modification aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Write the embodiment instruction as an addition to the inspection task, and withdraw the inspection under a post-modification effectivity condition.

expected_findings.rationale: The escape path marking strip is bonded across the floor panel joint line in the same zone. It cannot be lifted and refitted, so every aircraft that takes the strap change loses a length of marking that has to be replaced as a consumable.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the marking strip to the material list as a consumable and quantify the length per aircraft in the embodiment estimate.

expected_findings.rationale: The flight deck display installation runs its harness under the forward cabin floor in the same zone and needs the same panels lifted. One operator had the two changes booked into different visits, which was pure duplicated downtime.
expected_findings.resolution: Flag the access overlap to fleet planning and offer a combined embodiment package.

expected_findings.rationale: The fault isolation procedure sends the technician under the same floor panels to check a bonding path, and its access instructions name the panel numbers by the pre-modification fastener count. The strap change alters that count at two joints.
expected_findings.resolution: Correct the access instruction fastener counts in the same documentation package.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. No blocking item. The commercial finding was the alignment with the scheduled corrosion inspection, which halved the estimated retrofit cost per aircraft.
